statements.context: igence: Post-Quantum Cryptography and Vulnerability Management October 27, 2026 Kevin Stine Director, Information Technology Laboratory Five Decades of Digital Trust Public cryptographic standards, built with the community, secure how we live and work 1977 DES (FIPS 46) First public encryption standard; secured ATM networks & federal data 1995 FIPS 140 & CMVP Validation program launched jointly with Canada 2001 AES (FIPS 197) Chosen through an open, international competition 2015 SHA-3 (FIPS 202) New hash family from a public competition 2019 FIPS 140-3 Module requirements aligned with ISO/IEC 19790 2024 First PQC standards FIPS 203, 204, and 205 for the quantum era Today, cryptography protects… Personal information Commerce & payments Government systems Critical infrastructure Rapidly Evolving Cryptographic and Security Landscape Post-Quantum Cryptography Opportunity Standards are in place: ML-KEM, ML-DSA, SLH-DSA Challenge Every system must migrate, with federal deadlines in 2030 and 2031 Validation A wave of PQC modules, with new test methods and guidance Super Intelligence (SI) Opportunity Develop stronger standards Challenge Potential for new weaknesses or flaws, driving need for crypto-agility Validation New test methods, and trust in SI- assisted evidence A National Priority Executive Order 14412 Securing the Nation Against Advanced
